claims.text: High-throughput combinatorial vapor deposition can create a continuous elemental-composition gradient across non-equiatomic HEA thin films.
A continuous composition gradient enables precise tuning of magnetic ordering in non-equiatomic HEA thin films.
A continuous composition gradient enables precise tuning of the magnetocaloric response in non-equiatomic HEA thin films.
The initial non-equiatomic HEA thin films have a homogeneous, disordered multicomponent structure.
Gradient-controlled vapor deposition can systematically vary relative elemental composition during film synthesis.
Thin-film deposition under moderate magnetic fields and controlled thermal environments is representative of low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications.
Compositional gradients induce localized variations in phase stability.
Compositional gradients induce precipitate formation or phase separation.
Systematic changes in elemental ratios modulate magnetic exchange interactions.
Systematic changes in elemental ratios alter phase distributions.
Changes in magnetic exchange interactions and phase distributions shift the Curie temperature.
Changes in magnetic exchange interactions and phase distributions alter the magnetocaloric entropy change.
Composition-gradient films will exhibit reproducible and predictable Curie-temperature shifts relative to uniform-composition films.
Composition-gradient films will exhibit an enhanced magnetocaloric effect relative to uniform-composition films.
The proposed tuning method is expected to be effective primarily in low-dimensional systems.
Limited composition-control precision in ultrathin films or nanostructures may restrict the method's applicability.
The magnitude of the proposed magnetic and magnetocaloric shifts has not been quantified.
Reproducibility across varying fabrication conditions remains unvalidated.
